subject.title: Per-agent tools.selfDeny — allow tool inheritance to subagents while denying direct use

question: Should OpenClaw add a per-agent delegate-only/self-deny tool policy, and what public config shape and deny-wins semantics should own it?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but this changes how tool-deny security boundaries propagate from requester agents to subagents, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent API contract.

options.title: Approve delegate-only config
options.body: Add an optional per-agent policy that removes selected tools from the requester model surface while preserving them for controlled child inheritance unless normal deny policy blocks them everywhere.

options.title: Fold into per-spawn policy
options.body: Let `sessions_spawn.toolsAllow` own child narrowing and document that parent direct-use prevention still requires separate profiles, agents, or instructions.

options.title: Keep monotonic policy only
options.body: Reject parent-deny delegation and document the security rationale plus separate-agent workarounds.

recommendation.title: Approve delegate-only config
recommendation.body: Add an optional per-agent policy that removes selected tools from the requester model surface while preserving them for controlled child inheritance unless normal deny policy blocks them everywhere.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest available routing signal for a public config and security-boundary decision across agents and tool policy.
